final_message:
DONE. The P&L workbook is built, but I couldn't open it to check how it looks. LibreOffice isn't installed here, so I checked the figures by recalculating them in Python.

**Files in outputs/**
- `2024_Fall_Music_Tour_PL_as_of_2024-12-31.xlsx`

**What's in it**
- **P&L tab:**
  - "As of 12/31/2024" is in the header.
  - Columns are Tour Manager, Production Co. and Combined.
  - Revenue is shown gross by stop (all seven, by city and country), then withholding tax by stop, then net revenue.
  - Expenses are grouped into your four categories, followed by Net Income.
  - Currency is formatted in USD. Totals use live formulas.
- **Assumptions & Notes tab:** the withholding rates and the 11% commission rate, plus the assumptions below.

**Results**

| Item | Amount (USD) |
|---|---|
| Gross revenue | 1,043,750 |
| Withholding tax | 191,321.57 |
| Net revenue | 852,428.43 |
| Tour Manager expenses | 549,612.50 |
| Production company expenses | 182,393.00 |
| Total expenses | 732,005.50 |
| Net income | 120,422.93 |

The private jet is $341,000, which is about 47% of total expenses.

**Assumptions to confirm**
- Only the one reference workbook was in the folder. There were no other workspace records or a registry, so I used that file as is.
- All source amounts were already in USD, so I did no currency conversion.
- The production company reported costs only and no revenue, so its revenue column is zero.
- The 11% agency commission is calculated on gross revenue, as in the Tour Manager file. If the contract says it should be on net revenue, expenses would be lower.
- Petty Cash ($8,000) and Fees ($1,679) have no description in the source. I put them in Other Tour Costs. If any of it is travel, moving it changes the category split but not net income.
- I treated withholding tax as a deduction from revenue, not an expense. I did not estimate any US foreign tax credit recovery.
- No costs incurred after the tour through 12/31/2024 were provided, so none are included.
